meta.scope: Uruguay batch 6 — Deep international trade architecture (MERCOSUR external agenda, Singapore, EFTA, investment treaties, public procurement) and industrial/commercial promotion (zonas francas, investment promotion regime, logistics hub). Focused poke at deals and industrial side.

candidates.title: TLC MERCOSUR–Singapur
candidates.description: Free-trade agreement between MERCOSUR and Singapore. Modern agreement covering goods, services, investment and public procurement. Entered into force for Uruguay in March 2026.
referenced_by: MEF trade-agreement monitoring and origin-certificate reporting
candidates.notes: First MERCOSUR FTA with an Asian partner in force for Uruguay. Includes chapters on services, investment and public procurement. Continuously cited as a template for modern external agreements.

candidates.title: TLC MERCOSUR–EFTA
candidates.description: Free-trade agreement between MERCOSUR and the European Free Trade Association. Signed September 2025; complements the broader EU relationship.
referenced_by: Export strategy for European markets beyond the EU
Policy debate on agro-export and industrial access
candidates.notes: Completes the European preferential architecture alongside the MERCOSUR–EU interim agreement. Continuously cited in the external-agenda narrative.

candidates.title: ACE 35 MERCOSUR–Chile / bilateral Chile instruments
candidates.description: Economic complementarity agreement and related bilateral instruments with Chile, including public-procurement and origin-regime modernisation.
candidates.notes: Long-standing Pacific-facing instrument. Origin regime modernised in 2024–25; public-procurement agreement with Chile is among the earliest of its kind for Uruguay.

candidates.title: Acuerdos de Promoción y Protección de Inversiones (APPI / BITs)
candidates.description: Network of bilateral investment treaties (≈32 in force with 34 countries). Provides legal protection and, in a subset of cases, establishment rights for foreign investors.
candidates.notes: Core legal infrastructure for FDI. Treaties with the US, Chile and Japan include liberalisation (establishment) provisions; most others are post-establishment protection instruments.

candidates.title: Régimen de Zonas Francas
candidates.publisher: Dirección Nacional de Zonas Francas / MEF
candidates.description: Free-zone regime offering tax and customs incentives for industrial, commercial and services activities. Strategic instrument for logistics, manufacturing and global-services investment.
candidates.notes: Flagship industrial/commercial promotion instrument. ~11–14 free zones in operation. Protocol with Brazil (Additional Protocol 83 to ACE 18) allows zero-tariff entry of free-zone goods into Brazil subject to origin rules — a material industrial-competitiveness lever.

candidates.title: Ley de Promoción de Inversiones / COMAP regime
candidates.description: General investment-promotion regime granting tax benefits (IRAE, wealth tax, import duties, VAT credits) for declared investment projects. Administered through COMAP.
candidates.notes: Primary horizontal investment-incentive framework. Recent decrees have expanded 100% IRAE exemptions for large projects meeting employment and R&D/innovation criteria. Continuously cited in investor-climate materials.

candidates.title: Uruguay XXI — investment & export promotion agency
candidates.description: National agency for investment attraction and export promotion. Publishes investor guides, sector profiles and trade intelligence.
candidates.notes: Institutional interface between the international agreements / incentive regimes and private investors and exporters. Continuously cited in FDI and export-strategy analysis.

candidates.title: Acuerdos de Compras Públicas
candidates.description: Public-procurement market-access agreements (Chile, MERCOSUR Protocol with Brazil, chapter in MERCOSUR–Singapore FTA). Open government procurement to foreign suppliers under reciprocal terms.
candidates.notes: Commercial-side complement to goods and services trade agreements. Chile and Brazil instruments are in force; Singapore chapter is part of the broader FTA.

candidates.title: Protocolo de Zonas Francas MERCOSUR–Brasil (ACE 18 Adicional 83)
candidates.description: Additional protocol allowing goods produced in Uruguayan free zones to enter Brazil at zero tariff subject to origin rules. Material industrial-competitiveness instrument for free-zone manufacturing.
referenced_by: Uruguay XXI and free-zone investment materials
Industrial-location decisions for export to Brazil
candidates.notes: High-leverage industrial instrument. In force since 2022; frequently cited as the reason free-zone manufacturing can compete for the Brazilian market on equal footing with other regional hubs.

candidates.title: Relación comercial y estratégica con China
candidates.description: Strategic partnership and intensive bilateral trade relationship with China (top export destination). Includes dairy-protocol and broader economic cooperation; FTA negotiations and RCEP interest under discussion.
referenced_by: Export statistics (China often #1 destination for beef, soy, pulp)
Policy debate on Asia diversification and possible FTA/RCEP path
candidates.notes: De-facto structural trade partner. Continuously cited in export-performance analysis even in the absence of a comprehensive bilateral FTA; dairy protocol and strategic-partnership language are recurring reference points.

proposed_edges.basis: The Singapore FTA underpins preferential access and rules of origin for bilateral trade.
The EFTA agreement expands preferential European market access beyond the EU.
The Brazil free-zone protocol determines the tariff treatment of free-zone output in the Brazilian market.
The investment-promotion regime is administered under the MEF/COMAP framework.
Uruguay XXI promotes and explains the investment-incentive regime to foreign investors.
The BIT network is a core legal foundation cited in investment-promotion materials.
China is a top export destination; the bilateral relationship structures a large share of merchandise trade.
Public-procurement commitments are included in the MERCOSUR–Singapore FTA.
